findings.title: Gaza: MSF condemns another deadly attack on Nasser hospital
findings.location: Nasser Medical Complex, Khan Younis, southern Gaza Strip
findings.affected_population_system: Patients, healthcare workers, surgical and inpatient services at a major referral hospital serving an estimated 1.3 million people in southern Gaza
findings.exact_supporting_passage: The airstrike hit Nasser's surgery building, killing six people, including a child and a surgeon, and injuring 52 others.
findings.source_type: Primary humanitarian medical NGO field statement (MSF), indexed primary-source text; full direct open returned DisabledError
findings.confidence: moderate-high (primary MSF statement indexed; precise publication hour and direct page body not independently fetchable)

discovery_context.publication_novelty: MSF primary statement dated November 12 surfaced in this watch; publication time not available, so not claimed to have been issued strictly after previous heartbeat.
discovery_context.significance: MSF states 52 people were injured in the pre-existing Nasser strike, whereas the earlier AP report recorded at least 28 injured. Treat 52 as a revised reported total, NOT 24 separately confirmed new injuries. MSF additionally reports having operated on two wounded doctors and one other patient in a separate building; emergency, radiology, laboratory and operating departments remain out of service. These are quantified primary clinical observations of a previously recorded incident, not a second strike.
discovery_context.verification: First-party MSF page surfaced with full key paragraphs in indexed web search; direct page fetch failed (DisabledError). AP directly retrieved, reporting 6 deaths and at least 28 injured, with service suspension. Cross-report discrepancy is flagged; 52 has not been independently corroborated.
discovery_context.duplicate_guard: Previously logged Nasser Hospital strike (6 killed), earlier >=28 injury estimate, and suspended surgical/radiology/laboratory services are NOT counted as new incidents; only MSF's newly encountered injury total and first-hand treated staff/patient detail are promoted as follow-up.
